svg.title: Adaptive curriculum sequencer — layered architecture
svg.desc: A six-layer model: a fixed spine, standardized tags, a prerequisite graph gate, a purpose-weighted scorer that picks the next lesson, performance-adaptive insertion, and deferred engagement signals. Shows what to build now, soon, and defer.
svg.text: A playlist with rules — the sequencer in layers
free choice among prerequisite-satisfied lessons; hard rules underneath. build bottom-up.

g.text: Foundations: tones → alphabet → core A1 survival. Tones first, always. Hard-ordered.
replaces the linear getNextNode — chooses what comes after the spine
one pool, not 3 curricula. each lesson tagged:
candidate allowed only if every requires_*
tune the feel, no code change.
items due → insert SRS review session (getDueItems)
→ Next lesson, rendered on a visible path
SRS interval / due dates · answer streaks
response time · hesitation · quits · replays · speed
act on it only once data justifies it (fast ≠ bored)
Now — Layer 1 tag schema + Layer 2 prerequisite graph. Pure data, low risk, replaces 3 curricula with 1 tagged pool. It's what you asked for.
Soon — Layer 3 scorer (admin-tunable) + Layer 4 remediation & SRS surface. Rides on data + dormant code you already have.
Defer — Layer 5 engagement. Add logging now; postpone engagement-driven sequencing until the signals prove themselves.
Fixed — Layer 0 spine stays hard-ordered for everyone. Tones before vocab, no matter the purpose.
